answer.rationale: The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms cannot meet the 18% mandate, and defer_decision is not viable on an expiring critical contract (unlike the non-critical case in memory_c5). The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone, and memory_c2 indicates quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, supporting a switch. However, memory_c1 (integration stability with incumbent) and memory_c3 (single point of failure) flag real delivery risk: at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, a full cutover concentrates supply in one vendor and any onboarding slip stops the line. With only one decision slot, dual-sourcing alongside the switch is impossible this cycle; I am flagging this as the key downstream risk and verifying memory_c2 before committing, since the entire case rests on the low-cost vendor's proven reliability. Next cycle's priority should be qualifying a second source.
